name: Irs

subjectOf.text: The IRS position that virtual currency is taxed as property is expressly limited to convertible virtual currency, which leaves the tax treatment of crypto limited partnership interests unaddressed.
subjectOf.abstract: However, the IRS was very specific about limiting its current position to transactions involving "convertible virtual currency," leaving the tax treatment of crypto-limited partnership interests unaddressed.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Innovation for Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998033

subjectOf.text: Cryptocurrency gains are massively underreported to the IRS: despite Bitcoin rising from under twenty dollars in 2013 to over twelve hundred dollars in 2017, the IRS received only around 900 Form 8949 filings indicating crypto gain or loss over four years.
subjectOf.abstract: While the value of Bitcoin in 2013 under $20 and its value appreciated to over $1200 in 2017, in the past four years, the IRS has only received around 900 Form 8949 that would indicate some gain or loss from cryptocurrencies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Innovation for Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998033

subjectOf.text: The IRS confined its virtual currency position to transactions in convertible virtual currency, which leaves the tax treatment of crypto limited partnership interests unaddressed.
